titre_page: How to make a character walk, jump and climb without nodes? | Yop2D guide
description: Yop2D behaviors: a platform character that walks, jumps and climbs ladders, or a top-down character, with its animations, without a single node.
h1: Behaviors: a character that moves without nodes
carte: Walk, jump, climb, top-down view and animations, without a single node.
etapes: Choose "Platform character", controls "Joystick", and add a joystick.
Name them idle, walk, jump, climb and duck: the engine plays them by itself.
blocs: Before, making a character walk, jump and climb took a lot of nodes and formulas. Now you simply choose **what the object does** in the inspector's **⚙ Object behavior** window, and the engine does the rest.
a ground: an {{lang:obj_prefix_image}} or a wide, flat {{lang:obj_prefix_carre}} at the bottom of the scene;
a ladder (an {{lang:obj_prefix_image}}), if you want to climb;
a {{lang:obj_prefix_joystick}} at the bottom left of the screen.
In the inspector, tap the **⚙ Object behavior** button.
Choose **Ground / wall**: it doesn't move, you walk on it and bump into it.
For a platform you can jump through from below, also check **Pass-through from below** in the "It is also…" part.
In "Its settings", leave **Controls: Joystick**. You can choose the **Speed** and the **Jump height**.
Add a {{lang:obj_prefix_joystick}} to the scene. No need to choose a target: the character follows it by itself.
Run the game: the joystick makes the character walk, and pushing it up makes it jump.
Prefer a button to jump? Choose it in **Jump button**. Prefer ◀ ▶ buttons? Choose **Controls: Buttons**, then the left button and the right button.
Select the ladder and tap **⚙ Object behavior**.
Leave **Scenery** and check **A ladder** in the "It is also…" part.
Make the ladder go a little above the platform it leads to.
Run the game: in front of the ladder, push the joystick up to climb and down to go down. At the top, the character lands on the platform.
While climbing, the character doesn't fall: it stays hanging if you let go of the joystick. Push sideways to leave the ladder.

In the **Animations** window, give the character's animations these names: **idle**, **walk**, **jump**, **climb** and **duck**. The engine plays the right animation for what the character does, and flips the image when it goes left.
An animation is missing? No problem: the image just doesn't change in that case.
Several characters? Start the name with the object's name: **player_walk**, **enemy_walk**. Each one takes its own.
You can also choose the animation by hand: in "Animations played automatically", tap a line and pick from the list (with a thumbnail of each animation).
An enemy that walks by itself

For a patrolling enemy, also choose **Platform character**, but with **Controls: None**: it no longer obeys the joystick. Move it with your nodes (for example [[glisser_vers]]): it keeps gravity and its animations follow its real movements.
In **Directions**, choose **4** (up, down, left, right), **Iso view** (4 diagonals) or **Left / right**.
Name the animations with the direction: **walk_up**, **walk_down**, **walk_left**, **walk_right**, and **idle_up**… (in iso view: **walk_ne**, **walk_nw**, **walk_se**, **walk_sw**).
No "left" animation? The engine flips the "right" image.

The [[changer_comportement]] node offers the same choices as the window. Example: a crate set to **Ground / wall** starts falling when a lever is pulled: [[changer_comportement]] → **Falls and bounces**. Every setting left on "(don't change)" keeps its value.
Download the **Climb & run** (platform, ladders, animations) and **Dungeon walk** (iso view) examples in the **Examples** tab of Yop2D's home screen, then tap the hero and open **⚙ Object behavior**.
**The character doesn't move:** check **Controls: Joystick** (not "None") and that there is a joystick in the scene (or in the HUD).
**It falls through the ground:** the ground must be set to **Ground / wall**.
**It doesn't climb:** the ladder must have **A ladder** checked, and the character **Can climb ladders: yes**.
**The animation doesn't change:** check the animation names, or pick them by hand in the list.
